public_rationale: The surrounding text gives 'artificial revenue' a checkable meaning: dependence on outside financing. The financing announcement confirms investment, but it does not show how model purchases were funded or whether operating receipts could sustain them. The searched records do not settle the broad claim.
limitations: Funding, ARR, gross margin and operating cash flow are different measures.
One company's financing cannot establish dependence across the claimed population.
The cash-flow period and terminology require interpretation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI startups are an artificial source of revenue for AI labs because they pay with venture capital rather than cashflow.

statement.excerpt: AI startups are an artificial source of revenue.

from_speaker: AI startups are an artificial source of revenue
They are not paying Anthropic and OpenAI out of cashflow
only able to do so as long as somebody else hands them endless amounts of cash
our_interpretation: In context, 'artificial' means payments depend on outside financing because operating receipts cannot sustain the business and its model purchases. It is not read as an allegation of fabricated accounting revenue.
The plain reading concerns the venture-backed API customers discussed in the post.
I use the second calendar quarter of 2026, the latest completed quarter that could ordinarily have been reported before September 8. No reporting period is stated.
Raising venture capital does not by itself establish that model purchases could not be funded from customer receipts.
criteria.support_condition: Matched cash-flow and supplier-payment records show that the relevant startup customers could not sustain payments to the labs from operating receipts and depended on outside financing during the target quarter.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records show that a substantial portion of the relevant customers sustainably covered their model purchases and ongoing operations from operating receipts, making the broad funding-dependence claim false.
